Arabic fragrance encyclopedia and decant shop · Pre-seed 2026

Fragrantica speaks 21 languages. None of them is Arabic.

OurScent (عطرنا) is the fragrance encyclopedia of the Arab world — 64,294 perfumes in Arabic, English and French — with a shop on top that sells original perfume by the vial: 3, 5 and 10 ml decants filled from sealed bottles. Live at ourscent.online since September, selling in Egypt, and selling in Saudi Arabia since 10 November 2026.

The problem

The world's deepest perfume culture has no encyclopedia of its own.

Three gaps. Every one of them takes about a minute to verify.

Fragrantica publishes 21 language editions. Not one is Arabic.

Hebrew, Mongolian, Ukrainian and Greek each have their own. 46.6 million monthly visitors and 1.74 million members, and no Arabic front door — in the region that wears more fragrance per head than anywhere on earth.

Oud, attar, bukhoor and mukhallat are not categories anywhere.

A global database files a forty-year-old Hindi oud under "woody". No grade, no origin, no wild-versus-cultivated, no burn method. The part of the market Arab buyers care most about is the part no platform describes.

The way to try a perfume here is to buy the whole bottle.

An original bottle costs hundreds of riyals, the ratings a buyer reads were formed in a different climate, and the shop counter is a paper strip. Decants exist, but mostly as anonymous Instagram sellers with no record of which bottle the vial came from.

The product

An encyclopedia built in Arabic, with a shop that lets you try before the bottle.

Six things the platform does today, each of them live on ourscent.online.

Three languages, Arabic first

Arabic by default, English at /en and French at /fr, with the Egyptian edition at /eg written the way Egypt speaks. Every perfume, brand and note is published in all three, not translated on the fly.

The encyclopedia, open to everyone

64,294 perfumes with note pyramids, accords, concentration, year, perfumer, and oud and alcohol marked on every page. Free to read, and 61,871 of those pages are already in the sitemaps search engines read.

Original perfume, by the vial

3, 5 and 10 ml decants filled from sealed bottles, each carrying a LOT code and a QR back to the bottle it came from. A buyer tries a perfume for the price of a meal before committing to the bottle.

Ready-made boxes

Curated sets of vials — 20 on sale in Saudi Arabia and 14 in Egypt — for a buyer who wants to explore rather than choose.

Priced and delivered locally

Prices in SAR with 15% VAT and in EGP with 14%. In Saudi Arabia, Riyadh in one to two days for 20 SAR, the rest of the Kingdom for 35, free over 300; in Egypt, every governorate by Egypt Post. Sealed vials can be returned.

Content that posts every day

Reels, carousels and stories generated from the catalogue and published to Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, X and YouTube — 25 posts to Instagram alone between 1 and 11 November.

How it works

From open data to a shop that sells it.

Three stages. Two of them are live.

  1. 01

    Build the encyclopedia

    Open fragrance datasets merged, crawled and enriched into 64,587 records, of which 64,294 are published on the site in three languages. Live since 16 September 2026.

  2. 02

    Turn the reader into a buyer

    The decant shop on top of the encyclopedia: 53 perfumes in three sizes in Saudi Arabia, boxes in both countries, cash on delivery, VAT invoices and returns. Egypt was selling by early November; Saudi Arabia opened on 10 November.

  3. 03

    Let the community rank it

    Votes and the club — the part nobody can copy. The club is built and marked coming soon on the site; no votes are being collected yet. This is the stage the raise pays for.

Why this wins

A local edition is not a translation.

Three reasons a global platform cannot simply add Arabic and take this market. The table below is the evidence; these are the thesis.

It is a schema problem, not a wording problem

Adding Arabic to Fragrantica gives you Arabic labels on Western categories. It does not give you oud grades, attar subtypes or bukhoor burn methods — those are schema changes to a 119,000-row database that works fine without them, for an audience that rounds to nothing against 46.6 million visitors.

The votes do not port

A global longevity score is the average of everyone, everywhere. Re-voting a whole catalogue for Gulf heat, Ramadan and prayer is not a feature release — it is starting a community over. Whoever collects those votes first holds data the others cannot copy.

Selling vials is a local operation

Filling from sealed bottles, LOT codes, VAT invoices, a registered company per country, couriers and returns. A global website can add Arabic labels; it cannot add a Riyadh warehouse and a Saudi commercial registration.

The field

The competition is a good website people read in a second language.

Almost nobody here is choosing between Arabic fragrance platforms. They are choosing between reading English, watching a TikTok, and asking the man in the shop.

Who they areWhat they do well Where they stop
FragranticaThe de facto archive 119,000 fragrances, 2.3 million reviews, 1.74 million members and 46.6 million monthly visitors across 21 language editions. Two decades of community depth nobody can shortcut, and the reference this whole category is measured against.No Arabic edition, no oud grading, and no way to buy or try anything. Its ratings describe a European wardrobe, and an Arab buyer has to read them in a second language.
Parfumo and ParfumeiThe modern challengers Cleaner apps, barcode scanners, wear trackers and far better collection tools than the incumbent. Parfumei is influencer-first and moves quickly.The same Western catalogue with an English and German centre of gravity. Arab houses appear as entries in it, never as a category with structure of their own — so the fastest-growing part of the market is the part they describe least well.
TikTok and Snapchat reviewersThe real incumbent Where this market genuinely decides what to buy: Arabic, on camera, trusted, immediate and free. No platform we build competes with the trust a Gulf creator already has.Nothing is searchable, comparable or permanent. You cannot filter a video by halal status, sort it by price per millilitre, or find what a creator said about a fragrance eighteen months ago.
Instagram decant sellersThe closest thing to us Small sellers who split bottles and ship vials, in Arabic, often with cash on delivery. They prove the demand exists.No catalogue to research in, no record of which bottle a vial came from, no VAT invoice and no registered company behind the sale. Trust is the whole product, and they cannot show it.
Noon, Namshi and OunassWhere full bottles are bought The full regional catalogue at real prices, with Arabic storefronts and working logistics.Product pages, not an encyclopedia, and full bottles only. No notes pyramid, no community, and no way to try a perfume before paying for the whole bottle.

Stated fairly: a collector who reads English and buys full bottles from a mall is well served today. The wedge is the buyer who wants to try before spending hundreds on a bottle, in Arabic, from a seller who can prove where the perfume came from.

Market

A market that buys more fragrance per head than any other.

Sized on fragrance retail rather than on beauty as a whole, because the narrower number is the honest one.

Middle East fragrance retail $4.0B → $5.8B +7.5% CAGR · 2025 to 2030
Saudi Arabia — the largest share $1.9B → $2.7B +4.0% CAGR · 2024 to 2033

Market figures are third-party and are the only numbers on this page not drawn from our own repositories or the live site: the region from Expert Market Research ($3.76B in 2024, $4.04B in 2025, 7.5% CAGR), Saudi Arabia from IMARC.

Already built

What exists today, live and in files that can be opened.

This is the half of the work that does not demo well and cannot be skipped.

An encyclopedia of 64,294 perfumes, live

3,266 brands, 1,743 notes and 88 accord families in Arabic, English and French, with 61,871 perfume pages listed in the site's sitemaps. Built from 64,587 crawled and enriched records.

A shop that takes orders in two countries

53 perfumes in three sizes in Saudi Arabia — 159 products, all in stock — plus 20 boxes there and 14 in Egypt. Behind it: an order pipeline, VAT invoicing, a finance ledger, LOT and QR codes per vial, gift cards and returns.

The backend — FastAPI on Postgres, about 860 routes

One Python service with 143 database migrations and 158 test files, plus services for crawling, content, dupes, news, offers and a bottle recognizer that identifies a perfume from a photo.

Three front ends

A server-rendered React Router site with 136 routes, an operations dashboard of about 85 pages, and a Flutter app that is written but not yet published.

Distribution that already runs

A Google Merchant Center feed of all 159 Saudi products, Bing verification, an llms.txt for AI assistants, 16 sitemaps, and daily posting to five social networks.

The mechanism

Why each customer costs less than the last.

The encyclopedia brings the reader. The vial turns the reader into a buyer. The votes keep them.

The encyclopedia is the free front door

61,871 perfume pages in Arabic are 61,871 ways to be found by someone searching for a perfume — traffic that does not have to be bought.

The vial is the easy first purchase

A three-vial order is a small decision. A buyer who liked a vial already knows which bottle to want next, and where to research it.

One sealed bottle, many orders

Each bottle is split into vials sold to many customers, and every vial carries a LOT code back to it — so stock is traceable and the trust problem decant sellers have is solved by design.

The votes are still the asset nobody can copy

Gulf-climate longevity and occasion votes exist nowhere because nobody has asked. The club that collects them is built and not yet open; opening it is the next stage.

The model

Two ways it earns today, two it is built to add.

The shop holds stock and ships it — the opposite of the referral-only model this page described in September. The prices below are the live ones.

Decant sales · live

3 ml from 15.76 SAR, 5 ml from 26.27 SAR and 10 ml from 52.54 SAR, up to 372.34 SAR for a 10 ml vial of the most expensive perfume, with a minimum of three vials per order.

Ready-made boxes · live

Curated sets of vials — 20 on sale in Saudi Arabia and 14 in Egypt — at a higher order value than single vials.

Brand data and insights · not started

Which notes, climates and price bands Arab buyers respond to, sold back to the houses in aggregate once the votes exist. No personal data leaves the platform.

Full bottles and partnerships · not started

A buyer who liked a vial wants the bottle. Selling it, or referring it to a retailer, is the natural next line; no agreement is signed today.

Roadmap

What comes next, in order.

The first item is the gap between what is built and what is switched on.

  1. P1

    Switch on Saudi online payments

    Card payments through Paymob, with PayTabs as the fallback, and Tabby and Tamara instalments — built against sandbox accounts today. Plus courier booking through OTO and the last ZATCA e-invoicing step.

  2. P2

    Open the club and collect the votes

    Climate, occasion and longevity votes from Saudi and Egyptian buyers, with ratings shown only once there are enough of them to be real.

  3. P3

    Publish the app

    The Flutter app, written and running, released to Google Play and the App Store.

  4. P4

    Open the UAE

    The third market, once Saudi Arabia shows the model works. It is not registered today.

Honest state

What is true today, including the parts that are not flattering.

Written down before you check, because you will, and finding it yourself costs far more than reading it here.

LIVE

The encyclopedia and the shop are live

ourscent.online has been in production since 16 September 2026. Egypt has its own edition at /eg; Saudi sales opened on 10 November. ourscent.com is a separate, parked domain.

TOO EARLY

No traction figure is quoted

Saudi sales opened the day before this page was checked. Orders and revenue are below the threshold the platform publishes, so this page does not quote them. Social followings are small: 18 on Instagram and 20 on Facebook in late October.

COD ONLY

Saudi Arabia pays cash on delivery

Card payments and instalments are built against sandbox accounts and not switched on. Courier bookings in Saudi Arabia are made by hand.

REGISTERED

A registered seller in both countries

A Saudi company with a commercial registration and VAT number, and a registered company in Egypt, both shown on the site.

NOT IN STORES

The app is written, not published

The Flutter app exists and runs; it is not yet on Google Play or the App Store.

ONE PERSON

The whole thing is carried by one operator

Design, backend, all three front ends, the data pipeline, the shop and the content engine are one person's work. That is why it exists at this cost, and it is also the ceiling the raise is meant to lift.

The ask

$200K pre-seed, on a post-money SAFE.

Eighteen months from a shop that opened this month to one with online payments, an open community and the evidence to raise a seed round.

  • $200,000 — raising $150K to $250KA standard post-money SAFE, buying eighteen months of runway.
  • Payments, stock and operationsSwitching on Saudi card and instalment payments, courier integration, and the sealed bottles the vials are filled from.
  • Community and contentArabic fragrance creators in Saudi Arabia and Egypt to seed the club and the votes, and one content editor working in Arabic.
  • A second pair of handsOne engineer, so the single-operator risk named above stops being the ceiling on how fast any of this moves.
